rows.exact_current_claim:
## Statement

Fix a time and let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ for periods $L_j>0$ in metres, with the completed unnormalised pushforward $dx$ of Lebesgue measure on $\prod_j[0,L_j)$ as in the kinetic-density definition. Choose a constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the units of $f$, and let $f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to(0,\infty)$ be measurable in $x$, $C^2$ in velocity $v\in\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres per second, and integrable in velocity for almost every $x$. Let $Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{12}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra, and let $\nu$ be a locally finite symmetric measure on this set with full support, meaning every nonempty relatively open subset has positive $\nu$-measure. Use the collision domain and weak-test spaces of the elastic-collision definition; for almost every $x$, require $f(x,\cdot)\in\mathcal D_\nu$, so its four collision evaluations are $\nu$-measurable and all compactly supported smooth tests have the required absolute convergence in the weak identity. Define
$$D_x:=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}\bigl(f(x,v)f(x,w)-f(x,v')f(x,w')\bigr) \log\!\left(\frac{f(x,v)f(x,w)}{f(x,v')f(x,w')}\right)d\nu,$$
and assume $D_x$ is measurable and integrable. If $\int_\Omega D_x\,dx=0$, then for almost every $x$ there exist $C(x)>0$ with the units of $f$, $U(x)\in\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres per second, and $\theta(x)>0$ measured in squared metres per second squared, such that
$$f(x,v)=C(x)\exp\!\left(-\frac{|v-U(x)|^2}{2\theta(x)}\right)\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^3.$$
For almost every such $x$, the collision operator annihilates this profile in the weak sense that $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_\nu(f(x,\cdot))(v)\,dv=0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Conversely, every profile of this form has $D_x=0$; when it belongs to $\mathcal D_\nu$, the same compact-test weak identity gives this annihilation conclusion. Here $\theta$ has units of squared speed. The claim characterizes zero collision production only; it does not assert that a spatially varying Maxwellian solves the transport equation.

rows.exact_current_claim:
## Definition

Fix the particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and velocity Lebesgue measure $dv$ from the kinetic-density definition. Put $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$. Here $v\in\mathbb R^3$ is measured in metres per second, and $f$ is a number density in velocity space with units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. For a finite-valued nonnegative measurable velocity density $f:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ with finite absolute third moment $\int\omega_3(v)f(v)\,dv<\infty$, set $n:=\int f\,dv$. Where $n>0$, set $u:=n^{-1}\int vf\,dv$ and $T:=m(3k_Bn)^{-1}\int|v-u|^2f\,dv$; then $n$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $u$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $T$ has units kelvins. Define the admissible BGK input domain
$$\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}:=\left\{f:\int\omega_3f\,dv<\infty,\ f\ge0\text{ finite-valued measurable},\ n>0,\ \int|v-u|^2f\,dv>0\right\}.$$
For $f\in\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$, the temperature $T$ is strictly positive, $\theta:=k_BT/m$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$, and the moment-matched Maxwellian $M[f]$ and relaxation operator are defined by the following formulas; $M[f]$ has the same units as $f$:
$$M[f](v):=n(2\pi\theta)^{-3/2}\exp(-|v-u|^2/(2\theta)),\qquad Q_{\rm BGK}(f):=\frac{M[f]-f}{\tau}.$$
For fixed relaxation time $\tau>0$ measured in seconds, the displayed formula defines the single-species Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) relaxation operator pointwise on $\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$, with $Q_{\rm BGK}(f)$ in units of $f$ per second. The corresponding accelerated homogeneous model with dimensionless parameter $\epsilon>0$ is $\partial_t f=Q_{\rm BGK}(f)/\epsilon$. Outside $\mathcal D_{\rm BGK}$ this item assigns no BGK operator. This is a prescribed relaxation model. It is distinct from the binary collision operator and does not by itself assert a derivation from microscopic mechanics or an inhomogeneous hydrodynamic limit.

rows.exact_current_claim:
## Statement

Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$, let $\tau>0$ be a relaxation time in seconds, and let $\epsilon>0$ be dimensionless. Let $f_0:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable velocity density with $\int\omega_3 f_0\,dv<\infty$, number density $n=\int f_0\,dv>0$, and strictly positive centered second moment $\int|v-u_0|^2f_0\,dv>0$, where $u_0=n^{-1}\int v f_0\,dv$. Fix a constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f_0$, and assume $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,dv<\infty$, using $0\log0:=0$ and assigning $f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|$ the value zero where $f_0=0$. These are the hypotheses of the homogeneous BGK relaxation theorem; the fixed $m>0$ and $k_B>0$ and the Gaussian $M=M[f_0]$ are as in the single-species BGK definition. Set
$$f^\epsilon(t)=M+e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}(f_0-M),\qquad t\ge0.$$
For each nonnegative velocity density $g$ with the same units as $f_0$ and for which the integral is absolutely finite, define
$$H(g):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(v)\log(g(v)/f_{\rm ref})\,dv,\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
Then for every time $t\ge0$ measured in seconds,
$$0\le H(f^\epsilon(t))-H(M) \le e^{-t/(\epsilon\tau)}\bigl(H(f_0)-H(M)\bigr).$$
The lower bound is relative entropy with respect to the moment-matched Maxwellian. This is a deduction for the adopted BGK model and its explicit solution, not an empirical entropy measurement or a claim about the binary collision operator.
